subject: Request: onshore processing confirmation + operational artifacts for model-exemption
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@medanswer.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, procurement@medanswer.com
Cc: security@medanswer.com
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Onshore processing confirmation + model-exemption artifacts

Naomi / Redwood team,

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we can move the pilot forward I need to confirm two items for our InfoSec and procurement review:

1) Onshore processing: can you confirm that inference data for our pilot (customer identifiers, clinical notes snippets) can be processed and persisted only on US-hosted infrastructure (including any short-lived persisted KV or logs)? We need a simple statement of residency plus any operational controls you rely on (SFTP lanes, VPC tenancy, KMS region).

2) Model-exemption / no-model-improvement: our legal team needs operational artifacts showing that data will not be used to improve Redwood models (no adaptive training, no retention into model training datasets). Specifically they asked for:
  - a short runbook describing how capture/telemetry is gated and deleted,
  - subprocessor inventory with onshore/offshore flags,
  - evidence of KMS or HSM key residency and access controls, and
  - a sample DPA clause or redline that maps to what you can contractually commit to.

Can you provide those artifacts or point me to the certs/attestations you can share? If preferable we can do a 30-min call but procurement is on a tight cadence this week.

Appreciate a quick confirmation of what you can supply and a target ETA.

—Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Security & Compliance, MedAnswer
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@medanswer.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, procurement@medanswer.com
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onshore processing confirmation + model-exemption artifacts

Sanjay — thanks for the clear list. We can provide all of the artifacts you requested. High level:

- Residency: We can operate the pilot entirely on US-hosted infrastructure (single region: us-west-2) behind your VPC peering or our Dedicated tenancy depending on your preference. Short-lived KV caches and traces are stored only in-region and purged per the runbook below.
- No-model-improvement: Redwood supports a contractual "model-exemption" for this pilot — operationally we implement capture gating, ephemeral KV, and a denied ingestion pipeline to any training stores. We will provide an Ops runbook, a subprocessor inventory with location flags, a KMS residency diagram, and a suggested DPA redline for the no-training clause.

I've looped in David (platform/ops) and Kimberly (legal). David will attach the runbook and subprocessor inventory; Kimberly will share suggested DPA language and a DocuSign link for redlines. Connor is on the Dedicated deployment team if you want an architecture walkthrough.

Proposed next steps:
- We will send the artifact package within 24 hours (operations-runbook + subprocessor-inventory + KMS diagram + DPA redline).
- If those look good, propose a 30-min ops + legal call Tue or Wed to confirm wording and sign the DPA addendum.

Does Tue 11am PT or Wed 9am PT work for your team?

Thanks — talk soon.

Naomi Feldman
Head of Partnerships — Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@medanswer.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 13:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onshore processing confirmation + model-exemption artifacts

Sanjay / Naomi — attaching the operational artifacts we discussed (see attachment stubs below). Quick technical notes:

- Inference path: customer requests hit our gateway in us-west-2. Temporary KV cache is provisioned per-session and encrypted with a KMS key that is provisioned and region-scoped (us-west-2). Eviction: KV TTL by default is 1 hour for interactive sessions; for this pilot we will set TTL to 5 minutes and enable immediate explicit deletion after response emission. The runbook documents the purge operation and audit steps.
- Telemetry: request-level telemetry required for billing/observability (token counts, latency) will be aggregated and stored in an internal metrics pipeline that is configured to exclude payloads and PII. Any detailed traces that could contain prompt text are routed to an onshore SFTP drop which your team controls; we will not forward them to training stores.
- Subprocessors: the attached CSV lists the subprocessors and shows a column for "processing_region" (us/eu/apac). We will exclude any offshore subprocessors from the pilot or replace them with onshore alternatives for the pilot scope.

Attachments (stubs):
- operations-runbook.pdf (runbook: purge procedures, audit steps, TTL config sample)
- subprocessor-inventory.csv (list + processing_region + contact)
- kms-residency-diagram.png (diagram of key ownership and region scoping)

If you want a short walkthrough I can join the call and show the runbook flows.

—David
David Kim
Head of Platform Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@medanswer.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medanswer.com
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onshore processing confirmation + model-exemption artifacts

Sanjay — adding sample language we've used successfully with other healthcare customers. This is intentionally short so procurement can evaluate quickly: 

"Provider shall not use Customer Data, prompts, or model outputs for the purpose of improving, adapting, or retraining any machine learning, model weights, or model databases. Provider will implement operational controls (as described in the accompanying Operations Runbook) to prevent ingestion of Customer Data into any model-training datasets. Provider will supply an attestation and operational artifacts (subprocessor inventory, KMS residency diagram, and purge runbook) upon execution of this Addendum."

We can accept a limited carve-in if MedAnswer needs narrower exceptions (for example, anonymous telemetry for infrastructure debugging only) — we'll document any carve-in and require prior written approval.

I'll draft the DPA addendum redline and share a DocuSign routing link by EOD. If procurement prefers, we can accept the clause as an addendum to the existing DPA rather than a bespoke SOW.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@medanswer.com>, procurement@medanswer.com
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Mar 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onshore processing confirmation + model-exemption artifacts

Sanjay — attaching the consolidated package for your review (attachments listed below). Per the team: we will operate the pilot exclusively in us-west-2, exclude offshore subprocessors for the pilot, and enforce the model-exemption operationally via the runbook flows. Kimberly included suggested contractual language for the DPA addendum.

Attachments (actual files attached to this message):
- operations-runbook.pdf (details: TTL = 5 min, explicit purge command sample, audit checklist)
- subprocessor-inventory.csv (columns: name, role, contact, processing_region)
- kms-residency-diagram.png (shows customer-facing keys in us-west-2; Redwood-managed signing keys in separate partition)
- dpa-redline-clauses.docx (legal suggested addendum with no-model-improvement clause)

Next steps:
- Please confirm receipt and whether the DPA clause as drafted meets procurement's needs. If yes, Kimberly will route the DocuSign redline for signature (link: https://docusign.com/example/medanswer-dpa).
- If you want a technical walkthrough we can lock Tue 11am PT — David and Connor will join.

If procurement needs a narrower wording for telemetry exceptions, flag it here and Kimberly will prepare a limited carve-in.

Thanks for moving fast on this — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
